objective: Evidence-backed, implementable intra-round mechanical contract for the 1500 public full-log rounds in g0.txt, g1.txt, and g2.txt.

included: full-log grid decoding and render precedence

status_legend.confirmed: Directly specified by the official documents and/or reproduced without mismatch across every applicable full-log sample.
status_legend.inferred: Best implementation-level inference from exhaustive logs, but not fully fixed by an official statement or not exercised in every edge case.
status_legend.unknown: Not identifiable from these logs and official documents.

method.description: Parsed all 1500 round objects. Replayed every effective action in dispatch order, maintained a latent terrain/item board and actor positions, applied the arithmetic below, and rendered the expected end grid. Also checked every round-level ground and held-gold conservation equation.

steps.details: Actor positions and held player gold entering round r are prior end[r-1]. In the full logs, start.players, start.npcs, start.npc, and start.overlap_events are literal stale copies of the prior end fields for all 1497 inter-round transitions. Consequently start.actions and start.pickup describe the preceding round, not r.

Generate current-round gold and update bombs. The resulting board is start.grid and is the common pre-action board received by both players. Bomb sets were unchanged at all 1425 non-refresh boundaries and changed at all 72 boundaries with r > 0 and r % 20 == 0. Round 0 also starts with a sampled bomb set.
Both see the same pre-action world. Each returns six actions, split by k between unit 0 and unit 1, plus unit order and VP purchase. Full logs store current decisions only in end fields.
The lower current end.players[].cost acts first; an exact tie would dispatch P1 first by FAQ. Cost ordering matched dispatch_order in 1500/1500 rounds; no tie occurred.
All seven NPC ids occur once each in dispatch_order[1:8], between the two players. The observed NPC permutation is authoritative; its policy is outside scope.
The other player executes after all NPCs.
Write current-round actions, pickups, positions, player gold, events, burned amount, current cost/order, cumulative vision_spent, dispatch_order, and rendered end.grid.

player_group_atomicity.contract: Within a player dispatch, the unit selected by order executes its entire assigned action list, then the other unit executes its entire list. Units do not alternate actions.

vision_purchase.contract: VP bought in round r affects round r+1 for one round. vision_spent is cumulative and does not reduce gross in-game unit gold; final scoring subtracts it. Observed per-player-round increments were 0 in 2438 cases, 2 in 357, and 3 in 205.

generation_internal_order.details: Gold and bomb updates are jointly before decisions, but their internal random-sampling order is not observable. Their distributions and the outer-gold schedule are intentionally undisclosed.

full_log_grid_contract.warning: The full-log grid has actor overlay values -2 and -4 that are not part of the public GameInput grid table.

overlay_values.-2: one player unit on otherwise empty floor; owner is not encoded
overlay_values.-4: one or more NPCs on otherwise empty floor; also used when NPC and player overlap on empty floor

full_log_grid_contract.decode_to_latent_board: For a full-log grid value v: retain v when v > 0 or v is -1/-3; decode -2, -4, and 0 as empty latent floor.
render_precedence: wall or bomb where occupiable under the mechanics
full_log_grid_contract.implementable_renderer: If latent value is positive, -1, or -3, emit it. Otherwise, if any NPC occupies the cell emit -4; else if any player occupies it emit -2; else emit 0.

examples.conclusion: NPC overlay wins over player overlay on empty floor
gold wins over both actor overlays

bomb_overlay_edge.details: No phase snapshot had an actor on a bomb: entry consumes the bomb, and refresh avoids actors. Thus bomb-versus-actor visual precedence is not independently exercised, though the renderer above reproduces every end grid.

player.allocation: Each player has exactly six action slots per round. Unit 0 receives actions[0:k], unit 1 receives actions[k:6]. k may be 0..6.
player.execution: Apply each effective action sequentially. A successful 0..3 changes position by its delta. Action 4 leaves position unchanged.
player.blocking: A direction is blocked by out-of-bounds, a wall, or the current cell of any of the other three player units. NPCs never block players. On a block, that step does not move, but all later steps are still attempted from the unchanged position.
player.dynamic_occupancy: Only current positions matter. A vacated cell can be entered later in the round. Four player units cannot share a cell, pass through a currently occupied player cell, or swap through each other in one simultaneous operation because execution is sequential.

npc.execution: Each of seven NPCs has exactly three effective actions per round with the same 0..4 deltas. Bounds and walls block NPC movement. NPCs may overlap other NPCs and player units; none of those actors block an NPC.

effective_action_replay.answer: Yes. End-state positions replay exactly by treating logged end.actions as effective actions: add deltas for 0..3 and make 4 a no-op. Collision checks can be retained as assertions, but they must not try to move a logged 4. For exact pickups, bombs, tramples, and grid state, replay actors in end.dispatch_order and each player's end.order.
effective_action_replay.blocked_rewrite_caveat: The engine has already rewritten blocked directional attempts to 4. The original attempted direction is erased, and a literal strategy no-op is also 4, so those causes cannot generally be separated.

action_4_classification.interpretation: The no-blockable-direction cases prove that effective 4 is not exclusively a blocked-action marker. Cases with a possible blocker remain ambiguous because the erased direction is unavailable.

pickup.trigger: Only a successful move from one cell into another cell whose latent ground gold before entry is g > 0. Action 4 never picks up, even while standing on positive gold.
pickup.calculation: take = ceil(0.65 * g) = (65*g + 99) // 100; latent_gold = g - take
pickup.repeat_entry: Residual gold remains. Leaving and re-entering repeats the same calculation on the then-current residual.
pickup.generated_underfoot: Official FAQ says gold generated under a stationary actor is not automatically picked up. No such boundary occurrence was observed in these three games.

bomb.player_trigger: On successful entry to a bomb cell, penalty = ceil(0.10 * current_unit_gold) = (gold + 9) // 10; subtract it from that unit and remove the bomb. Later actions continue.
bomb.npc_trigger: NPC entry also removes the bomb. NPC cost stayed 0 and no NPC-held purse or NPC bomb penalty is exposed.
bomb.sampling: At round starts divisible by 20, including round 0, the bomb set is sampled/refreshed before decisions. Surviving bombs otherwise persist until entered. Refresh does not merely top up: old bombs are removed and a new set appears, with occasional coincident cells.

examples.conclusion: NPC consumed the traversed bomb and continued to [8,2]

trample.trigger: After each successful player move, count NPCs currently on the destination. If count >= 3, apply a penalty on every such entry. NPCs arriving later do not retroactively penalize a stationary player.
trample.calculation: After any pickup on that same step, penalty = ceil(0.05 * current_unit_gold) = (gold + 19) // 20.
trample.event_frequency: Two triggers, both in g0 enclosing round 496. They are distinct repeated entries and must not be deduplicated even though their event objects are identical.

coin_plus_trample_order.basis: Official FAQ explicitly says pickup precedes trample. The two logged tramples did not also pick up gold, so that combined edge was not empirically exercised.

burned.definition: end.burned is the current round's total player gold destroyed by bomb penalties plus trample penalties, not bomb-only loss.
burned.equation: sum(start player unit gold) + sum(end current-round player pickups) - end.burned = sum(end player unit gold)
burned.evidence: Exact in 1500/1500 rounds. Total burned 5736 = 5706 bomb + 30 trample.

mutual_exclusion.contract: Official FAQ says one cell cannot simultaneously contain bomb and gold, nor bomb and >=3 NPCs. Bomb refresh avoids actors, NPCs, gold, and old bombs.

dispatch_contract.shape: [faster_player_id, seven negative NPC ids in execution order, slower_player_id]

cost_unit.details: Only ordering is needed for mechanics; the full logs do not label the numerical unit of cost.

file_layout: line 2: 17x17 matrix of strings describing a static map layer; value '1' aligns with walls, while the purpose of '2' is undocumented and unnecessary for replay
following 500 lines: one JSON round object each

phase_common.players: array of two PlayerState records, ids 1 and 2
phase_common.npcs: array of seven NpcState records with stable negative ids
phase_common.npc: redundant exact alias/copy of npcs[0] in 3000/3000 phases
phase_common.overlap_events: array; always empty in all 3000 phases

PlayerState.cost: int; current decision cost in end, prior-round stale value in start
PlayerState.gold: int; sum of the two unit gold fields
PlayerState.order: int 0 or 1; current choice in end, stale in start

UnitState.actions: array of effective ints 0..4; current round only in end
UnitState.pickup: int aggregate current-round pickup only in end

NpcState.id: stable negative int -1..-7, list order is game-specific
NpcState.actions: exactly three effective ints 0..4 in end
NpcState.pickup: int aggregate current-round pickup in end
NpcState.cost: int; observed 0 in all 10500 end records

end_only.burned: int current-round aggregate destroyed player gold

TrampleEvent.round: int using 1-based display numbering; equals enclosing round + 1 in both observations
TrampleEvent.unit_owner: int player id; unit index is not included
TrampleEvent.penalty: int gold destroyed by this trigger

OverlapEvent.details: No non-empty overlap_events entry occurs, so its element schema and intended semantics cannot be recovered. Do not use it to infer legal player/NPC overlap.

state_freshness_contract.authoritative_current_round_fields: Use end.actions, end.pickup, end.cost, end.order, end.positions, end.gold, end.burned, end.trample_events, and end.dispatch_order for round r. start.grid is current pre-action truth after generation; start actor positions/gold are valid pre-action state even though the enclosing actor records carry stale action/pickup metadata.
state_freshness_contract.npc_total_rule: Sum only end.npcs[*].pickup once per round. Never combine start and end pickups.

definitions.ground(phase): sum of all positive values in phase.grid; positive gold renders above actors, so this is exact

material_balance.vision_note: vision_spent is excluded from physical gold conservation because in-game gold fields are gross. Apply vision_spent only to final score.

mismatch_examples_and_traps.name: stale start pickup
mismatch_examples_and_traps.example: g0 round 1 start NPC -5 has actions [2,3,0] and pickup 3, exactly g0 round 0 end. Its current round-1 pickup is 4 in round 1 end.
mismatch_examples_and_traps.impact: Treating start.pickup as current-round truth shifts or duplicates extraction. Summing start NPC pickups gives 5198/7049/6902 instead of the corrected end-only 5216/7051/6916.

mismatch_examples_and_traps.name: effective action 4 is not a direction to revalidate
mismatch_examples_and_traps.example: g0 round 0 P1 unit 0 replays [1,1,4] from [0,0] to [2,0]. The final 4 is a no-op in the effective stream; later actions would still execute if present.
mismatch_examples_and_traps.impact: Trying to infer and execute an erased blocked direction diverges. Apply 4 as no-op.

mismatch_examples_and_traps.name: NPC action 4 exists
mismatch_examples_and_traps.example: g2 round 4 NPC -7 has [4,0,1]. Across all logs NPC action 4 occurs 1806 times.
mismatch_examples_and_traps.impact: A replay that assumes NPC actions are only 0..3 fails.

mismatch_examples_and_traps.name: grid actor markers do not hide gold
mismatch_examples_and_traps.example: g0 round 105 end [7,15] contains P2 unit 1 and NPC -5, but grid is 2, not -2 or -4.
mismatch_examples_and_traps.impact: Positive cells must be preserved as latent ground gold even when occupied.

mismatch_examples_and_traps.name: NPCs consume bombs
mismatch_examples_and_traps.example: g0 round 18 NPC -1 traverses bomb [8,3] and continues to [8,2]; the bomb is gone.
mismatch_examples_and_traps.impact: Leaving bombs in place after NPC entry causes end-grid divergence.

mismatch_examples_and_traps.name: burned includes trample
mismatch_examples_and_traps.example: g0 enclosing round 496 has burned 30 and two trample penalties of 15, with no bomb loss needed for the balance.
mismatch_examples_and_traps.impact: Interpreting burned as bomb-only overstates unexplained loss.

mismatch_examples_and_traps.name: event round is display-numbered
mismatch_examples_and_traps.example: Both trample objects inside zero-based round 496 carry round: 497.
mismatch_examples_and_traps.impact: Use the enclosing round for replay indexing; retain the event field verbatim for schema fidelity.

mismatch_examples_and_traps.name: no residual simulator mismatches
mismatch_examples_and_traps.example: The stated contract reproduced all 1500 end grids and all 433500 cells exactly.
mismatch_examples_and_traps.impact: Any implementation mismatch on these logs indicates ordering, stale-field, overlay, NPC-bomb, or arithmetic handling differs from this contract.

steps: Initialize player/NPC positions and player unit gold from round.start.
Decode latent cells from start.grid: preserve positive, -1, -3; map -2/-4/0 to empty.
Read current effective actions, player order, costs, pickups, and dispatch from round.end, never from start.
For each actor id in end.dispatch_order: for a player, execute the ordered unit's full list then the other list; for an NPC, execute its three actions.
For action 4 do nothing. For 0..3, assert the effective move is legal, change position, then apply destination effects.
On positive gold apply ceil(65%). On a bomb remove it and, for a player, apply ceil(10%). After a player move, if current destination NPC count is at least 3, apply ceil(5%) after pickup.
Accumulate per-actor pickup and round burned; compare against end fields.
Render gold/terrain first, then NPC -4, then player -2, then 0; compare against end.grid.

unresolved_ambiguities.details: Blocked attempts are rewritten to 4, while literal no-op also records as 4. The erased direction and exact blocked-vs-voluntary split cannot be recovered.

unresolved_ambiguities.topic: NPC policy and dispatch permutation policy
unresolved_ambiguities.details: The logs expose only realized actions and order. Prediction is intentionally excluded.
Sampling counts, probabilities, and the outer-generation schedule are not public and vary across games. Only timing and realized deltas are replayable.

unresolved_ambiguities.topic: NPC hidden purse and bomb penalty
unresolved_ambiguities.details: NPC pickups remove ground gold and NPCs consume bombs, but logs expose no cumulative NPC gold. npc.cost is always 0. Whether an internal NPC purse is penalized has no observable effect on these replayed player/end-grid mechanics.
The second file line is not needed for round replay; only string value 1 clearly aligns with walls.
No sampled phase contains an actor on a bomb because bomb entry consumes it and refresh avoids actors, so this visual precedence is not directly observable.

unresolved_ambiguities.topic: coin plus trample on one step
unresolved_ambiguities.details: Official FAQ fixes pickup before trample, but no logged trample also had coin pickup; this edge is document-confirmed rather than log-exercised.
FAQ fixes P1 first; zero cost ties occurred in 1500 rounds, so this edge is document-confirmed rather than log-exercised.
